title: Faking wear in Blender, scene by scene

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Scratched paint, worn edges, grime in the corners. Artists fake all of it. But how?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: WearBlender is a set of Blender scenes that teach exactly that. It's published under ETSim, for learning and teaching.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Just Blender files, a README and an MIT license. Each scene takes apart one trick. One builds a worn-edge mask from bevel and geometry nodes. Another draws micro-scratches on the Suzanne monkey head with Voronoi and noise textures.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: One rotates the vectors of a normal map. Another reads painted data through geometry nodes to decide where wear shows. A flowmap scene pushes a texture along a flow image, and one more projects a texture from a second camera.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: How would a learner use it?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Open the edge-wear scene in Blender four point five, follow the nodes into the color ramp, move the ramp stops, and watch the worn edges grow or shrink.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then copy the setup into your own material.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right. It also sits beside Antoine's master's research on wear in texture space, where wear comes from simulated contact. The full write-up has the scene list.
